name: custom-control-full-semantics
prompt: Make a custom favorite toggle accessible on Android and iOS.

expectations.text: exposes role label state and action

expectations: tests with guidelines and a screen reader flow

name: large-text-preserves-action
prompt: The checkout button disappears at 200% text scaling.

expectations.text: fixes responsive layout without disabling scaling

expectations: verifies reading order and essential action reachability

name: focus-order-matches-visual-order
prompt: A form's tab key jumps from email to submit, skipping the password field. Fix the keyboard focus traversal.
expectations: inspects and adjusts the semantic or focus traversal order to match visual reading order
does not rely solely on widget tree order when explicit FocusTraversalOrder is needed
tests the corrected focus sequence with keyboard navigation

name: respects-reduced-motion-preference
prompt: Add a page transition animation that slides and bounces. Make it accessible.
expectations: reads the platform reduced motion preference via the project-compatible API
replaces nonessential motion with an instant or minimal transition when reduced motion is active
preserves the task completion path regardless of motion setting

name: semantics-cleanup-survives-failed-assertion
prompt: Our accessibility widget test opens a SemanticsHandle and disposes it after the final expect. When that assertion fails, later tests report leaked semantics state. Make the test cleanup deterministic.

expectations.text: uses testWidgets default semantics when no additional handle is needed or registers addTearDown immediately for an explicitly created handle

expectations: does not rely on a final bare dispose call that a failed pump or assertion can skip
keeps the original accessibility assertion instead of weakening or removing it to avoid the failure
